ai.title: Claude prompt caching in file selection
ai.summary: File selection prompts now pass full message history, system prompt, and tools to Claude for prompt caching. `requestRelevantFiles` accepts a structured object instead of raw messages, enabling reuse of cached context across Haiku and Sonnet calls. `mainPrompt` propagates these parameters through `updateFileContext`. Changes affect `backend/src/claude.ts`, `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, and `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system needs to pick out which code files are relevant to your request, it now keeps track of the whole conversation, your instructions, and the available tools all at once instead of sending them piece by piece. This means follow-up requests about the same files don't have to re-explain everything from scratch, so the file-picking step works faster on subsequent looks. You'd notice this mainly if you trigger multiple file-selection steps in a row, since the later ones build on context already gathered rather than starting over.

ai.title: Switch to Sonnet for non-obvious file requests
ai.summary: File request strategy updated to use Sonnet model for identifying 'non-obvious' files, replacing Haiku's 'comprehensive' approach. Logic in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` now prompts for files beyond the obvious choices. `common/src/util/changes.ts` adds existence check before unlinking files during change reverts to prevent errors on missing files.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to find files for a task, it now uses a smarter model to look for less-obvious files instead of casting a wide net. If you noticed the assistant missing some files before, it may now spot a few more relevant ones. Behind the scenes, when undoing changes, it double-checks that a file is really there before deleting it, preventing errors when a file is already gone. These changes are live today.

ai.title: Test asserts commentid and isAdmin in delete-comment.ts
ai.summary: Manifold project tests now verify `delete-comment.ts` patches reference `comment_id` and `isAdmin`. Logic changed to map file paths to patch content via `Object.fromEntries` for direct string inclusion checks. Scope limited to `backend/src/__tests__/manifold-project.test.ts`. Ensures generated code maintains correct authorization and identifier usage.

eli5.text: The system now checks that when a comment is deleted, it correctly uses the comment's unique ID and verifies the user is an admin, similar to checking a ticket number and security badge before removing a post. The verification is run by an internal testing process that simulates the deletion action in a safe environment, applying and then reverting the change to confirm everything works. This is purely a behind-the-scenes quality check that developers run automatically; you won't see any difference in the app, but it helps ensure deleting comments works properly and only authorized users can do it.

ai.title: Improve long path handling in file request prompt
ai.summary: Updated `request-files-prompt.ts` to handle long paths better by adding `topLevelDirectories` and `getExampleFileList` helpers. The prompt now explicitly instructs the model to correct relative imports to full root paths and includes shuffled example file lists to guide selection. Scope limited to backend file context logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks you to point it at files, it can now deal with projects that have very long folder paths without getting confused. The prompt it sends you now tells the assistant to use full paths instead of shortcuts, and it shows a shuffled list of example files so you can pick from them more easily. If you use the file picker today, you'll get a cleaner set of options when your project folders are nested very deeply. The change is live now for anyone using the internal file-request flow.

ai.title: CLI executes terminal commands and updates prompt
ai.summary: CLI intercepts user input to execute terminal commands directly via `handleRunTerminalCommand` before triggering AI processing. The `handleRunTerminalCommand` function in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` now accepts a `mode` parameter to distinguish between 'user' and 'assistant' execution, suppressing specific console logs and timeout kills for user-initiated commands. The CLI prompt in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` displays the project root basename. Backend file request logic in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` no longer skips file requests for terminal command inputs.

eli5.text: When you type a command meant for the terminal (like running a build or installing a package), the assistant now runs it right away instead of first asking for code files to look at. The command line still shows your project's folder name, and the assistant's own commands remain quieter (no blue echo line) so the two kinds of commands don't look the same. This is already live, so from your side it's just commands executing immediately and the prompt showing the folder name.

ai.title: Exclude knowledge.md files from request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Instruction added to request-files-prompt.ts to prevent LLM from selecting knowledge.md files. Assumes default inclusion of these files. Internal backend change.

eli5.text: You might have noticed the assistant repeatedly offering to open files named something like 'knowledge.md'. Those files are now skipped, since they get pulled in automatically anyway, so the list the assistant proposes should stop looking cluttered with entries you didn't ask for. The change went into the file that builds that list of files.

ai.title: CLI terminal commands now track working directory state
ai.summary: Internal refactor of CLI tool handling to persist current working directory across terminal commands. Replaced hardcoded `cd ${getProjectRoot()}` prefix in `handleRunTerminalCommand` with dynamic `cwd` tracking via new `getCurrentWorkingDirectory` and `setCurrentWorkingDirectory` functions in `project-files.ts`. Updated `cli.ts` to refresh the readline prompt base directory after command execution. This ensures `cd` commands executed by the agent correctly update the context for subsequent commands.

eli5.text: When you run a sequence of terminal commands, the system now remembers which directory you navigated to with cd, so the next command runs in the right place instead of always jumping back to the project home. You would notice that after typing cd subfolder, the directory name shown in your prompt changes to reflect where you are now. This works only inside the agent's CLI tool, so it mainly affects the automated workflow handling terminal commands during tasks.

eli5.text: The text you see from the assistant while it is typing now appears in blue instead of plain text. The folder name shown as your prompt is now green, and it automatically reflects whichever folder you are currently in. If you ask for help with a question word like 'what' or 'which', the system treats it as a request rather than a command to run.

ai.title: Only change dir on successful command
ai.summary: handleRunTerminalCommand now checks exit code === 0 before updating working directory. Prevents state corruption when cd fails. Scope: npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: When you use the terminal inside the assistant, the system now only updates your current location if your command succeeds. If a command to change directories fails, it no longer pretends the move worked and leaves you in the right spot. This prevents confusion if the command didn't actually complete.

ai.title: Add tests to dockerignore and ignore dep to common
ai.summary: Added `__tests__` to `backend/.dockerignore` and `ignore: 5.3.2` to `common/package.json` dependencies. Excludes test directories from Docker images and introduces the ignore library to the shared core package. Affects backend containerization and common module dependencies.

eli5.text: When the system builds the backend's deployment package, it now skips including any test files, which keeps the final image smaller and prevents test-only code from shipping to production. The shared code library also picked up a small helper for ignoring files by name pattern, letting the common module filter out entries without writing custom logic. If you rebuilt the backend today, you'd notice a cleaner image with no stray test folders, and the shared library now relies on a maintained dependency instead of an ad-hoc filter.

ai.title: Add ignore dependency to backend
ai.summary: Added ignore 5.3.2 to backend/package.json dependencies. Enables file path filtering in backend services. Scope limited to backend package.

eli5.text: The backend services now include a tool that lets the system skip over certain files when looking through a list of files, so only relevant ones are processed. Engineers building backend features can use this to filter out files that shouldn't be included in a given task. Nothing changes for end users right away; this just adds the filtering capability behind the scenes.

ai.title: Update main-prompt.ts to preserve existing code and comments
ai.summary: Instruction in backend/src/main-prompt.ts now explicitly directs preservation of existing code, comments, and behavior while limiting edits to core requirements. This ensures the agent avoids unnecessary modifications. Scope limited to the main prompt configuration.

eli5.text: The system now tells its assistant more clearly to leave existing work untouched, changing the instruction from 'make as few changes as possible' to 'preserve as much of the existing code, comments, and behavior as you can.' This affects anyone who relies on the assistant to make small, targeted edits without accidentally rewriting or stripping out comments in the middle of files. If you were to look at this change, you'd see the assistant is now instructed to be more conservative about what it modifies, keeping the original structure and explanations intact unless a change is truly needed.

ai.title: Token counter uses gpt-4o tiktoken encoding
ai.summary: The backend token counter now calls `encoding_for_model` with `gpt-4o` instead of `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`. The change fixes the model used for token counting in `backend/src/util/token-counter.ts`. The selected tiktoken encoding alias moves from a dated snapshot to the base model name.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal counter for how much text it processes has switched to a newer reference model, so token estimates stay in sync with the latest model version. This runs automatically in the background when the assistant tallies up text length. If you watch your own usage metrics, the numbers it reports now match the current model rather than an older dated snapshot. Most people won't notice a visible difference day to day.

ai.title: Fix import path and reduce deploy sleep
ai.summary: Corrected import path in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` to `common/project-file-tree`. Reduced VM readiness sleep in `backend/deploy.sh` from 60s to 10s. Affects internal build and deployment scripts.

eli5.text: The deployment process will now wait 10 seconds instead of 60 seconds for the virtual machine to start up, which means internal staff will see faster deployment times when pushing updates. Additionally, a small correction was made to how the application locates certain internal project files, ensuring they load correctly during builds. These changes only affect internal tooling and deployment scripts, so external users won't notice any difference in their experience. The fix is live today and impacts only the internal team managing deployments.

ai.title: Bump backend and npm-app to 1.0.48
ai.summary: Incremented version numbers in `backend/package.json` and `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.47 to 1.0.48. Pure version bump. No code changes.

eli5.text: The software quietly updated its own version labels to a newer number, a routine housekeeping step that does not add new features or fix bugs you can see. Two packages that make up the system, the backend server and the main application, both moved from 1.0.47 to 1.0.48, and if you opened their configuration files you would see only two version-number lines change in each. No other code was altered, so anything you experience in the app stays exactly the same.

This applies when Claude is acting on your behalf and the system detects either a 'command not found' or a 'syntax error' message, so confusing terminal errors won't leave you hanging.

If you looked at the project structure, the testing materials would now live in their own area instead of mixed in with the application code. This is purely a behind-the-scenes cleanup that improves how the code is organized and keeps test-only files from being included in the final product build.

ai.title: Remove filelist tags in request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Removed `<file_list>` XML tags from file extraction logic and prompts in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. Direct response parsing replaces regex matching to handle plain text file lists. Limit increased from 6 to 10 files for crucial request prompts. Internal change affects backend file retrieval mechanism.

eli5.text: The system that figures out which files to share with you when you ask a question has gotten simpler and a little more generous. Instead of wrapping its list of files in special tags that had to be carefully opened and closed, it now just reads each file path line by line, which is more reliable when something goes wrong. It also allows up to ten files to be suggested in the most important situations, up from six, so you get a bit more context when you need it. You won't see the tags anymore if you ever peeked at how the file suggestions were packaged behind the scenes.

ai.title: Parallelize file request prompts
ai.summary: Replaced single sequential LLM calls with parallel batches for key and non-obvious file requests in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts`. `getRelevantFiles` now accepts user prompt directly; `generateNonObviousRequestFilesPrompt` and `generateKeyRequestFilesPrompt` take `count` and `index` to shard requests. Results merged via `Promise.all` and `uniq`. Internal refactor.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to figure out which files in your project are relevant to a request, it used to ask for them one at a time, waiting for each answer before moving on. Now it splits that work into multiple smaller requests and sends them all at once, then combines the results, so the behind-the-scenes file gathering finishes noticeably faster. This is purely internal housekeeping: you won't see a new button or option, but tasks that lean on the assistant reviewing your project files should complete a bit more quickly. The change is already in place and active today.

ai.title: Clarify updatefilecontext tool description
ai.summary: Updated the `update_file_context` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts` to explicitly restrict usage to reading existing files. The new text clarifies that the tool selects from the set of existing files and must not be used to create new files. This change applies to the backend tool definitions.

eli5.text: The text describing a tool that helps the assistant pick which existing files to look at was rewritten to make its limits explicit. The tool now only lets the assistant add or remove files already present for reading, and the description states it should not be used to create new files. If you watched the assistant choose files, you wouldn't see different behavior today, but the written guidance telling it not to create files is now stricter and clearer than before.

ai.title: Add warm-context-cache action and prompt refinements
ai.summary: New `warm-context-cache` client action triggers a dummy prompt to pre-warm the system prompt cache. `getSystemPrompt` now accepts an options object with `onlyCachePrefix` to isolate cacheable content. File selection prompts in `request-files-prompt.ts` are tightened to enforce strict newline-separated output.

eli5.text: When you open the app, it warms up its response cache by sending a test question and then deleting the answer, so your next search starts faster. The developer comments note they do this even if it takes too long, they just give up and move on. File selection prompts were also tightened to only show exact file paths, no extra text. This change is live for all users today.

ai.title: Fix files service random commentary
ai.summary: Added filter to reject lines with spaces in getRelevantFiles. Appended 'Ignore previous instructions' to prompts for non-obvious and key project files. Prevents model from outputting commentary instead of file paths. Changes isolated to backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: When the system asked for project file suggestions, the assistant sometimes replied with commentary instead of just file paths. The assistant now rejects any suggestion line that contains a space, so only clean file paths are returned. Prompts for non-obvious and key file requests now end with 'Ignore previous instructions' to keep the assistant focused on outputting paths only. If you looked, you'd see fewer stray explanatory lines mixed in with your file lists.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.50
ai.summary: Incremented version to 1.0.50 in backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Internal release preparation.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was quietly raised to a new release number across the two parts of the software that track versions. You wouldn't notice anything different as a user. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping to prepare for an upcoming release.

ai.title: Fix relative imports in websocket-action.ts
ai.summary: Replaced absolute `src/` paths with relative `../` paths for `tools`, `system-prompt`, and `claude` in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`. Ensures correct module resolution within the backend package structure. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The backend had a mix-up in how it located some of its internal building blocks; it was looking for them in the wrong spot. The engineering team corrected those references so they point to the right place, and as a result, the system now finds and uses those building blocks properly instead of erroring out. If you were watching the logs, you might have seen failures related to loading tools, prompts, or the assistant engine; those should stop happening now. Nothing about what you see or do has changed, but the feature you are using becomes more stable under the hood.

ai.title: Add .manicodeignore support to project file tree
ai.summary: Added `.manicodeignore` parsing to `parseGitignore` in `common/src/project-file-tree.ts`. The function now checks for and applies patterns from this file alongside `.gitignore`. Leading slashes in `.manicodeignore` entries are stripped before being added to the ignore instance. This allows Freebuff to respect project-specific ignore rules distinct from git.

eli5.text: The assistant's project file browser now respects a project-specific ignore list (a.manicodeignore file) in addition to the standard.gitignore. When looking at a project's files, it skips anything listed in either file, so project authors can hide their own private folders (like __mock-projects__) without changing Git settings. If you check a project that has this file, those extra items simply won't appear in the tree view.

ai.title: File tree depth indicator replaces tabs
ai.summary: printFileTree in common/src/util/file.ts switches from tab-based indentation to numeric depth prefixes. The system prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts clarifies that numbers denote directory depth. This compresses the file tree representation.

eli5.text: When you open a project, the list of files and folders now shows a small number in front of each item instead of using blank space to push deeper items farther right. The number tells you how many folders deep that file or folder sits, one is right at the top level, two means it's inside one folder, and so on. This makes the file list shorter and easier to read, and the explanation of what the numbers mean appears right above where the list is shown. If you're used to seeing the old indented layout, this one-line-per-entry view is what you'll notice.
